_about: LanWatch NZ internet provider (ISP) knowledge base: the routers/modems each common New Zealand provider supplies, how to open their settings, and the provider's own help pages. Checked against the providers' help pages in November 2026; providers change their modems, so the label on the router is always the final word. A router model is recognised from the router's name (name_match, lower-case pieces). Used by app/services/router_advice.py. ADVICE ONLY: LanWatch never logs in to the router.

spark.name: Spark
spark.note: Spark's help site has a support page for each of its modems (settings, Wi-Fi and factory reset).

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.254 into a web browser.
routers.login: The factory login is admin / admin (also printed under the Wi-Fi sticker on the back), which is exactly why it should be changed.

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.254 into a web browser.
routers.login: The factory login is admin / admin (printed under the Wi-Fi sticker on the back). Change it.

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.254 into a web browser.
routers.login: The factory login is admin / admin; the modem asks you to change it the first time you log in.

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.254 into a web browser.
routers.login: Use the login printed on the modem's label, then change it.

skinny.name: Skinny
skinny.note: Skinny is part of Spark, and its help pages are on Spark's website.

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.254 into a web browser.
routers.login: The factory login is admin / admin; the modem then makes you choose a stronger password (8+ characters with a capital letter, a number and a symbol).

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.254 into a web browser.
routers.login: The factory login is admin / admin. Look for a password change option under the admin or system settings.

one_nz.name: One NZ (formerly Vodafone NZ)
one_nz.note: One NZ has guides for updating the Ultra Hub's firmware and for factory resets on its help site.

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.1 into a web browser.
routers.login: Use the login printed on the label underneath. If you changed it and forgot it, a factory reset puts it back (and also resets your Wi-Fi name and password).

routers.open: Type http://192.168.1.1 into a web browser.
routers.login: Use the login printed on the modem's label, then change it.

2degrees.name: 2degrees
2degrees.note: 2degrees also runs Orcon and Slingshot. Several of its newer modems are managed through an app rather than a web page.

routers.open: Most settings: the Nokia WiFi app. Web page: the address on the sticker underneath.
routers.login: The web page's 'admin' password is on the sticker underneath the modem.
Set up through the Aginet app; protect that account with a strong password.

routers.open: Type http://fritz.box into a web browser.
routers.login: The FRITZ!Box password is on the label underneath.

orcon.name: Orcon
orcon.note: Orcon is now part of 2degrees, and its help pages are on 2degrees' help site.

routers.open: Type the address on the modem's label into a web browser.
routers.login: NetComm modems have several logins; change the 'admin' and 'support' passwords.

routers.open: Type the address on the modem's label into a web browser.
routers.login: Use the login printed on the label, then change it.

slingshot.name: Slingshot
slingshot.note: Slingshot is now part of 2degrees, and its help pages are on 2degrees' help site.

routers.open: Type the address on the modem's label into a web browser.
routers.login: There are three logins. Slingshot recommends changing only the 'admin' and 'support' passwords.

routers.open: Type http://fritz.box into a web browser.
routers.login: The FRITZ!Box password is on the label underneath.
Set up through the TP-Link app; protect that account with a strong password.
Set up through the Deco app; protect that account with a strong password.

routers.open: The NF18ACV uses http://192.168.20.1; for the NF20, type the address on its label into a web browser.
routers.login: The NF18ACV's factory login is admin / admin, which should be changed.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.note: LanWatch doesn't have details of Mercury's modems yet: use the address and login on the modem's label, and Mercury's help centre.

other.name: Another provider / my own router
other.note: Use the address and login on the router's label, or the maker's app. The steps below work for almost every router.
